title: Incident #103: Slow gen_server:init/1 Blocking Supervisor Startup
solutionExplanation: Resolves supervisor boot timeout incident INC-103 by returning {continue, {hydrate, SeedRules}} from init/1 in 0ms and compiling firewall rules inside handle_continue/2.

otpDocCards.description: Invoked by gen_server immediately after init/1 or handle_call/cast returns {..., {continue, Continue}}.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Executed before any message in the process mailbox is dispatched.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why does moving heavy startup logic into handle_continue/2 fix supervisor timeout crashes?

options.label: start_link returns {ok, Pid} to the supervisor immediately, allowing the supervisor to complete child registration while hydration proceeds without blocking boot.
options.explanation: Correct! The supervisor child registration completes in microseconds, preventing supervision timeouts during rolling releases.

options.label: handle_continue runs on a separate remote computer.
options.explanation: handle_continue runs inside the same local BEAM process.

options.label: It increases the supervisor timeout from 5 seconds to 10 minutes.
options.explanation: Supervisor timeouts are not modified; the initialization latency is removed.

incidentAlert.symptom: During rolling deployments, the root supervisor times out and aborts boot whenever the firewall rule list exceeds 5,000 entries.
incidentAlert.impact: Cluster nodes fail health checks and get killed by Kubernetes during rolling updates, causing service outages.
incidentAlert.rootCauseHint: incident_blocking_init:init/1 performs synchronous rule compilation and normalization directly inside init/1 before returning {ok, State}, blocking gen_server:start_link/3.
incidentAlert.fixObjective: Refactor init/1 to return {ok, #{status => booting, raw => SeedRules, rules => #{}}, {continue, {hydrate, SeedRules}}} immediately, and move rule compilation into handle_continue({hydrate, SeedRules}, State) setting status => ready.
